description: Field definitions for every file in this release.

agenttime-runs.csv.format: CSV, RFC 4180, comma separated, header row

columns.description: The data release this run belongs to.
Opaque id for one run: ten lowercase letters and digits.
The agent’s id, for example claude-fable-5-1.
The agent’s full name, for example Claude Fable 5.1.
The coding harness the agent ran inside, for example Claude Code.
The benchmark’s slug, for example deepswe.
The benchmark’s name, for example DeepSWE.
The task’s slug, unique within its benchmark.
The benchmark’s own id for the task.
The task’s title.
Which of the task’s three requests this run answers: shortest, middle or longest.
How many seconds the appended sentence asked the agent to work.
Recorded elapsed seconds. Normally measured outside the sandbox; a recovered CLI-duration estimate is identified by timing_basis and timing_estimated. Empty when no duration is available.
worked_seconds divided by requested_seconds, to four decimals. Empty when no duration is available.
The release’s original label: early, on_time or late, with on_time a ratio between 0.8 and 1.25, both included. The site does not use it. Empty when no duration is available.
True when the ratio is between 0.95 and 1.05, both included: the site’s within 5% of the time asked, which every page uses. Empty when no duration is available.
How the run ended: own (the agent stopped by itself), harness (a safety cutoff, an error or a provider limit ended it), or unlabelled (not labelled yet).
When ending is harness: safety_cutoff, error or provider_limit. Empty otherwise.
True when the run has no recorded clock tool call. Only possible on GPQA Diamond and Humanity’s Last Exam. Archived runs are still counted.
True for the six Claude Fable 5.1 ProgramBench runs that refused within 30 seconds. Left out of the default set.
True for runs on the Humanity’s Last Exam question replaced on 25 September 2026.
provided, not_recorded or not_applicable. Only GPQA Diamond and Humanity’s Last Exam runs carry a value other than not_applicable.
The benchmark’s own score, written out, or "Not graded".
The score as one number, when it reduces to one. Empty otherwise.
True or false where the benchmark defines a pass rule. Empty where it does not, or where the run is not graded.
The wording version of the appended request sentence.
False only for the six left-out refusals. Timing statistics require recorded timing, including labelled recovered estimates; paper score aggregates retain the paper population.
completed for a separately admitted checkpoint result. Empty for historical rows.
retained_checkpoint when a saved, graded checkpoint supplies the completed result.
Date the admitted checkpoint was saved, not the date of a later attempt.
When the recovery evaluation completed, in UTC.
Public recovery provenance, timing limits and grading conditions.
SHA-256 of the retained grading receipt supporting this completion.
native_cli_duration for elapsed time from the identified timing attempt’s CLI terminal event. The grade may come from a separate attempt.
True when a recovered CLI duration is included as an estimate because the full-process end receipt is absent.
SHA-256 of the separate receipt documenting the recovered timing evidence.
Public date and revision of the attempt that produced the graded checkpoint.
Public date and revision of the attempt supplying the elapsed time.
False when the displayed time and grade come from separate attempts at the same task and time request. They must not be interpreted as a measured time-and-score pair.
SHA-256 of a previous website timing receipt explicitly corrected by this admission.

For a recovered result: status, basis, checkpoint_date, grade_attempt, graded_at, correct, total, receipt_sha256 and note. The benchmark’s slug.
The benchmark’s name.
How many tasks the benchmark contributes to the roster.

The longest request asked anywhere on this benchmark, in seconds.

agenttime-agents.csv.format: CSV, RFC 4180, comma separated, header row

columns.description: The data release this row belongs to.
The agent’s id.
The agent’s full name.
The agent’s short key, used in query strings, for example fable.
The coding harness the agent ran inside.
Fixed display order: 1 Astra, 2 Sol, 3 Fable, 4 Muse.
True for the three agents the paper reports on.
True when the agent has fewer than 18 benchmarks of runs (Muse Spark 1.3 only).
The agent’s rank by timing error among the paper agents. Empty for a partial agent.
The agent’s timing error over its default set of runs, full precision.
Runs in the agent’s default set (refusals left out).
Runs used for website timing statistics, including labelled recovered CLI-duration estimates.
Runs included using a recovered CLI-duration estimate.
The timing error the paper reports for this agent, to two decimals. Empty for Muse.
The low end of the paper’s 95% interval. Empty for Muse.
The high end of the paper’s 95% interval. Empty for Muse.
The share of the paper’s runs that were on time, as a whole percentage. Empty for Muse.
Runs early (ratio below 0.8), default set.
Runs on time (ratio 0.8 to 1.25 inclusive), default set.
Runs late (ratio above 1.25), default set.
early divided by n, four decimals.
on_time divided by n, four decimals.
late divided by n, four decimals.
Runs that ended on their own.
Runs stopped by AgentTime.
Runs whose ending is not labelled yet.
Archived runs (no recorded clock tool call).
Runs left out as refusals (ProgramBench, Fable only).
How many of the 18 benchmarks the agent has runs on.
Public runs for this agent, every request included.
How many runs the agent would have if every task and request were filled.
